benign.definition: Kind and gentle; not harmful or dangerous.
benign.example: "The lump proved benign," the vet assured Maya, "so your cat needs only rest."

ebb.definition: To decrease or become less, especially in strength or intensity.

replenish.definition: To fill something up again or make it full after it has been used.

exasperate.definition: To make someone very annoyed or frustrated.
exasperate.example: The scholar's endless revisions began to exasperate even his most loyal assistants.

petulant.definition: Easily annoyed and often complaining, like a child.
petulant.example: "Don't be petulant about one low mark," said Idris; "ask the teacher how to improve."

banish.definition: To send someone away or make them leave a place, often as punishment.
banish.example: I try to banish distractions by leaving my phone downstairs while I revise.

conservative.definition: Someone who prefers traditional values and is cautious about change.
conservative.example: Why does our conservative neighbour, so wary of change, own the street's most modern telescope?

emphatic.example: Why did the umpire's emphatic signal end the argument before it truly began?

profound.definition: Very deep or intense; having a strong effect or meaning.
profound.example: The philosopher's years in exile had a profound effect on everything he wrote afterwards.

counterargument.definition: An argument that opposes or disagrees with another argument.
counterargument.example: Writing the counterargument first actually strengthened my own position in the end.

implore.definition: To ask someone very seriously and urgently to do something.
implore.example: The villagers sent their elders to implore the king for protection from the raiders.

reprieve.definition: A temporary break from something difficult or unpleasant.

ecstatic.example: I was quietly ecstatic when my essay on Ibn Battuta won the regional competition.

justify.definition: To give reasons or explanations so that something makes sense.
justify.example: How do you justify spending public money on statues while the library roof leaks?

abate.definition: To become less strong or decrease in amount.
abate.example: The famine did not abate until the new irrigation channels reached the southern fields.

circumference.definition: The distance around the edge of a circle.
circumference.example: The club debated the circumference of social justice.

barter.definition: To exchange goods or services for other goods without using money.
barter.example: At the school fair I chose to barter my paintings for books rather than sell them.

roil.definition: To make something messy or disturbed, especially water or a situation.
roil.example: Rumours of the treaty's collapse began to roil the markets in every port city.

habitation.definition: A place where people or animals live.
habitation.example: Archaeologists found evidence of human habitation stretching back six thousand years.

liberal.definition: Open to new ideas and willing to change traditional beliefs.
liberal.example: She dismissed it all as liberal chatter.

unsightly.definition: Not pleasant to look at; ugly or unattractive.

defect.definition: A problem or fault in something that makes it not work properly.

initiative.definition: The ability to start something on your own without being told.

connoisseur.definition: A person who knows a lot about something and can judge its quality.

disposition.definition: A person's usual mood or way of thinking.

systematic.definition: Done according to a plan or system; organised and methodical.

cache.definition: A hidden store of things, often used to keep items safe.

strenuous.definition: Requiring a lot of effort and energy.

conclusion.definition: The final part of something where you summarise or decide what it means.

waver.definition: To be unsure about something or to change your mind.
waver.example: Did the young captain ever waver when the storm scattered half of his fleet?

abandon.definition: to stop doing, using or supporting something completely, often suddenly.

ability.definition: the power or skill needed to do something well.

abrupt.definition: happening suddenly and without warning, so that it feels unexpected or incomplete.

absorb.definition: to take something in gradually, especially information or ideas, until it becomes part of what you know.

academy.definition: a school or college, often one that specialises in a particular subject or skill.

accents.definition: distinctive ways of pronouncing words, typical of a particular region, country or social group.

accidents.definition: unexpected events, often causing harm or damage, that happen without being intended.

accord.definition: An agreement or harmony between people or groups.

according.definition: as stated or reported by a particular person, text or source.

accordion.definition: a portable musical instrument played by pressing keys or buttons while squeezing it in and out.

accounts.definition: spoken or written reports describing what happened during a particular event.

accustom.definition: To make someone familiar with something through repeated experience.

achieve.definition: to succeed in doing or reaching something, usually after effort.

activities.definition: things people do, especially for enjoyment, exercise or a particular purpose.

activity.definition: something that a person does, especially involving physical or mental effort.

actors.definition: people who perform roles in plays, films or other productions.

actual.definition: real or true, rather than imagined, claimed or expected.

adept.definition: Very skilled or good at something.

adjective.definition: a word that describes a noun, giving more information about a person, thing or idea.

adjusted.definition: changed slightly, especially to make something fit new circumstances or work better.

admirable.definition: deserving respect or approval because of a good quality, such as effort or courage.

admire.definition: to feel respect and approval for someone or something, often because of a quality you value.

adults.definition: fully grown people, no longer children.

adversary.definition: A person or group that opposes or fights against another.

affects.definition: has an influence or effect on someone or something.

affix.definition: To attach or stick something to another thing.

affluent.definition: Having a lot of money and wealth.

afford.definition: to have enough money to be able to pay for something.

afternoon.definition: the part of the day between midday and evening.

afternoons.definition: the parts of the day between midday and evening, on more than one occasion.

afterwards.definition: at a later time, after something else has happened.

against.definition: in opposition to something, in contrast to a background, or used to compare one thing with another.

agreeing.definition: reaching the same opinion as someone else, or accepting a proposal, usually after discussion.

agreement.definition: a shared understanding or arrangement between two or more people or groups about what should happen.
agreement.example: The debate lasted a full hour before anyone reached an agreement.

ahead.definition: in front, forward, or still to come in the future.

aid.definition: help given to someone, especially in a difficult situation or emergency.

aimed.definition: directed towards a particular target, group or purpose.

aims.definition: things that a person or group is trying to achieve; goals or purposes.

alarm.definition: a feeling of sudden fear or worry caused by possible danger, or a device that makes a loud warning sound.

alert.definition: paying close attention to what is happening, and ready to react quickly if needed.

alley.definition: a narrow street or passage, often between or behind buildings.
alley.example: "See how the balconies jut over the alley," said the guide; "storytellers once performed beneath them."

allot.definition: To give or set aside a certain amount for a specific purpose.
allot.example: We want to allot time each week for open dialogue, Amal explained.

allotment.definition: a small piece of land that a person rents to grow vegetables, fruit or flowers.
allotment.example: "Weeding is tedious until you notice the robins following you," smiled the allotment veteran.

allowed.definition: gave permission for something to happen or be done.

allowing.definition: giving permission for something to happen, especially while limiting or controlling it.
allowing.example: The instructor cautiously tested each stone before allowing the students to cross.

almost.definition: very nearly, but not completely or exactly.

alone.definition: on its own, without anyone or anything else present or involved.

aloof.definition: Not friendly or not interested in talking to others.

aloud.definition: using a voice that can be heard, rather than silently or in your head.

alpine.definition: relating to high mountains, especially the Alps, or found in high mountain regions.

alternatives.definition: other things or options that can be chosen instead of what is usual or expected.
alternatives.example: What is the strongest argument against replacing all plastic packaging with glass alternatives?

amazed.definition: filled with great surprise or wonder.
amazed.example: Kofi stared at the switchboard, amazed it hadn't broken yet.

ambassador's.definition: belonging to an official sent to represent their country in another country or organisation.

ambulances.definition: vehicles specially equipped to carry sick or injured people quickly to hospital.

amiable.definition: Friendly and pleasant to be around.

amiss.definition: not quite right; something is wrong or not as it should be

among.definition: surrounded by, or included as part of, a group of people or things.

amount.definition: a quantity of something, especially one that can be measured or counted.
amount.example: Would you trade a healthy coastline for a small amount of gold?

amounted.definition: added up to, or was effectively the same as, something, especially when judged overall.

amused.definition: caused someone to feel entertained or find something funny.

analysis.definition: The process of studying something carefully to understand it better.

analyst.definition: a person whose job is to examine information in detail in order to understand or explain it.

angry.definition: feeling or showing strong annoyance or displeasure.
angry.example: A patient advocate wins more support than an angry one.

animals.definition: living creatures, other than plants, that can move about and sense their surroundings, such as mammals, birds and fish.

animators.definition: people who create moving pictures or films, especially by making drawings or models seem to move.
animators.example: How long did the animators need to build such an intricate opening sequence?

ankle.definition: the joint connecting the foot to the leg.
ankle.example: Ouch, Sami, that ant just bit my ankle!

anniversary.definition: the date each year that marks when an important event happened in an earlier year.
anniversary.example: Coastal Rise planned a bonfire to celebrate the campaign's first anniversary.

announced.definition: made something known publicly, often for the first time.
announced.example: How stunned were you when the results were finally announced?

announcement.definition: a public statement giving information about something.
announcement.example: Who read the announcement to the rest of the class?

annual.example: Posters flapped against walls, advertising the annual Innovation for Impact challenge.

another.definition: one more, or a different one, of the same kind.

answer.definition: something said, written or done in response to a question or problem.

answered.definition: gave a reply or solution to a question, problem or need.

answering.definition: giving a reply or response to something, especially a question.

answers.definition: things said, written or done in response to a question or problem.

antagonise.definition: To make someone angry or upset by your actions or words

antics.definition: Funny or silly actions or behaviours that people do.

antonym.definition: a word that means the opposite of another word

anything.definition: any thing at all, of any kind.

anywhere.definition: in, at or to any place.

apart.definition: separated by a distance, or not joined or together.

apologised.definition: said sorry for something done wrong.

apology.definition: a statement expressing regret for having done something wrong.

appeal.definition: a public request for help, money or support for a cause.

appear.definition: to become visible, or to start to exist or be noticed.

appeared.definition: became visible or noticeable, or started to exist.
appeared.example: The organiser's name never appeared on the poster.

appears.definition: becomes visible, or starts to exist or be noticed.
appears.example: Anger switches off patient thinking almost the moment it appears.

applauded.definition: showed approval by clapping the hands.

applause.definition: clapping of the hands by a group of people to show approval or enjoyment.

apprehend.definition: To understand or grasp something; to catch someone who has done wrong.

apprehensive.definition: Worried or anxious about something that might happen.

apps.definition: computer programs designed to run on smartphones or other mobile devices.

aptitude.definition: A natural ability to do something well.

aqueduct.definition: a large structure, often like a bridge, built to carry water across a valley or gap.

archive.definition: a collection of historical documents or records kept for future reference.

archives.definition: collections of historical documents or records kept for future reference.

archivists.definition: people whose job is to organise and look after collections of historical documents or records.

ardent.definition: Showing strong feelings or enthusiasm for something

articles.definition: pieces of writing on a particular subject, published in a newspaper, magazine or website.

articulate.definition: To express thoughts and ideas clearly and effectively.

artistry.definition: great skill in creating something, especially in painting, music, writing or performance.

ascent.definition: an act of climbing or moving upwards, especially up a mountain or hill.

dishonest.definition: not truthful or fair; intended to deceive.
dishonest.example: A beautiful cover cannot make a dishonest story true.

dishonesty.definition: behaviour that is not truthful or fair; the practice of deceiving others.
dishonesty.example: What kind of dishonesty sullies an audience's trust the fastest?

dislike.definition: to feel that you do not like someone or something.
dislike.example: I dislike labels that obstruct the recycling symbol, because hiding it discourages proper sorting.

dismal.definition: sad and gloomy; not cheerful or happy
dismal.example: The once dismal grey river began to run clear again after years of clean-up.

dismissed.definition: refused to consider something seriously; rejected it.
dismissed.example: She dismissed it all as liberal chatter.

dispatch.definition: To send something or someone to a place quickly.
dispatch.example: How quickly can the shop dispatch a replacement string if we order it tonight?

dispel.definition: To make something go away, especially a feeling or belief.
dispel.example: The librarian organised a workshop to dispel the myth that poetry must always rhyme.

display.definition: to show something publicly so that people can see it.
display.example: Watch out, Nora, you nearly bumped the whole display!

displayed.definition: shown publicly so that people could see it.
displayed.example: The museum displayed a portrait of the young queen.

dispose.example: Which of these survey questions is actually pertinent to how families dispose of batteries?

dispute.definition: a disagreement or argument between people or groups.
dispute.example: The referee's decision settles every dispute on the pitch.

disrespect.definition: a lack of respect or consideration for someone or something.
disrespect.example: The elders defended an older doctrine which taught that questioning tradition showed disrespect.

dissent.example: Nora's voice was edged with dissent from Kian's carelessness.

dissipate.definition: To gradually disappear or become less strong.
dissipate.example: Why does stage fright dissipate the moment the first note finally sounds?

distant.definition: far away in space or time.
distant.example: A narrow path wound across the slope towards the distant ridge.

distract.definition: to take someone's attention away from what they are doing or thinking about.
distract.example: An elaborate set can sometimes distract from a simple story.

distracted.definition: had their attention taken away from something.
distracted.example: The band's gaudy costumes distracted the audience from an otherwise flawless performance.

distractions.definition: things that take a person's attention away from what they should be focusing on.
distractions.example: I try to banish distractions by leaving my phone downstairs while I revise.

distracts.definition: takes someone's attention away from what they should be focusing on.
distracts.example: "Hand in pristine copies," the teacher requested, "because smudged work distracts the moderators."

district.definition: an area of a town or region, especially one defined for administrative purposes.
district.example: Theo was the surprise winner of the district chess tournament.

dived.definition: jumped or plunged into something, or became fully and suddenly involved in an activity.
dived.example: I dived headlong into learning the ney flute, practising until my neighbours begged for mercy.

divided.definition: caused people to disagree, or split into different groups or opinions.
divided.example: The story's bizarre twist, revealing the narrator as a parrot, divided our class completely.

dizzying.definition: so high, fast or extreme that it makes you feel unsteady or disoriented.
dizzying.example: Who carried the water, stone by stone, to build a citadel at such a dizzying height?

dock.definition: an area or structure where ships load and unload goods or passengers.
dock.example: The filthy puddle near the dock smelled of oil and rubbish.

doctrine.definition: a set of beliefs or ideas that are taught by a group or organisation
doctrine.example: How can a community update its doctrine of stewardship without losing the wisdom inside it?

document.definition: to record something in writing or another permanent form, as evidence or reference.
document.example: Is that document part of the public record now?

documentaries.definition: factual films or television programmes about real events or subjects.
documentaries.example: I take copious notes during documentaries so I can quote exact figures in my essays.

documentary.definition: a film or programme giving a factual account of a real subject or event.
documentary.example: Whose turn is it to present the documentary next?

documentation.definition: written records or evidence about something.
documentation.example: I believe careful documentation gives endangered dialects a better chance of longevity than luck ever could.

doesn't.definition: a short form of 'does not', used to say that something is not the case or does not happen.
doesn't.example: The rumour runs wild online, doesn't it?

dogs.definition: common four-legged animals often kept as pets, as in the idiom 'raining cats and dogs'.
dogs.example: I love collecting bizarre English idioms, like raining cats and dogs, and tracing their strange origins.

doing.definition: carrying out or performing an action or task.
doing.example: You're doing brilliant work with the recycling scheme, Amal.

dome.definition: a rounded roof or ceiling shaped like half a ball.
dome.example: The final chord seemed to dissipate slowly into the dome of the concert hall.

dominance.definition: the state of having the most power, influence or control over something.
dominance.example: Could refill shops eventually usurp the supermarkets' dominance over how we buy household basics?

dominated.definition: had the most power, influence or presence over something.
dominated.example: Why are teenagers increasingly indifferent to banner adverts that once dominated every website?

don't.definition: a short form of 'do not', often used to tell someone not to do something.
don't.example: They arrive tomorrow, don't they, Nora?

donated.definition: gave something, especially money or goods, to help a person or cause.
donated.example: Several artists from the town donated paintings for the same exhibition.

donation.definition: a gift, especially of money, given to help a person or cause.
donation.example: The fundraising campaign gathered momentum once the local bakery offered to match every donation.

donations.definition: gifts, especially of money, given to help a person or cause.
donations.example: The charity's succinct slogan, just four words long, raised more donations than any leaflet.

done.definition: completed or carried out; the past participle of 'do'.
done.example: At last, Amal, justice has been done!

donkey.definition: a sturdy animal similar to a small horse, with long ears, often used to carry loads or riders.
donkey.example: Rescue workers fed the emaciated donkey until its strength returned.

door.definition: a hinged or sliding barrier that opens and closes an entrance to a room, building or vehicle.
door.example: The locker door stuck, just like it always did.

doors.definition: hinged or sliding barriers that open and close entrances to rooms or buildings.
doors.example: A good education opens many doors later in life.

doorstep.definition: the step or flat surface just outside the entrance to a house.
doorstep.example: Muddy paw prints on the doorstep were the telltale evidence of the fox's nightly visits.

doubles.definition: becomes twice as much, as many or as long as it was before.
doubles.example: "Consider this weekend a reprieve," said the coach, "because training doubles on Monday."

doubling.definition: making something twice as much, as many or as large as it was before.
doubling.example: Some brands feign concern for the planet while quietly doubling their plastic output each year.

doubt.definition: a feeling of not being completely certain about whether something is true, right or will happen.
doubt.example: Doubt clouded Kian's mind after he heard the rumour.

doubted.definition: was not sure whether something was true, or did not fully believe a claim.
doubted.example: Whereas you doubted the story, Kian, I believed it instantly!

doubts.definition: feelings of uncertainty about whether something is true, right or will succeed.
doubts.example: Watch her eyebrow, Leo — it always gives away her doubts!

downstairs.definition: on or towards a lower floor of a building, especially the ground floor.
downstairs.example: I try to banish distractions by leaving my phone downstairs while I revise.

downstream.definition: further along a river, in the direction that the water is flowing.
downstream.example: Untreated waste ended up destroying the fishing grounds downstream.

dozens.definition: many groups of about twelve, used loosely to mean a large number of things.
dozens.example: The station received dozens of emails after the broadcast aired.

draft.definition: an early or first version of a piece of writing, made before it has been corrected or completed.
draft.example: Amal erased her first draft and started the summary again.

drafting.definition: writing an early, unfinished version of a piece of text.
drafting.example: "Ignore the impending deadline for a moment," said Maya, "and simply enjoy drafting the story."

drafts.definition: early, unfinished versions of a piece of writing, made before the final one.
drafts.example: Mentors help young writers see the potential in their earliest drafts.

dragons.definition: huge mythical reptiles, often shown with wings, scales and the ability to breathe fire.
dragons.example: "Don't brandish the rake like a sword," laughed the gardener, "it's for leaves, not dragons."

drains.definition: pipes or channels that carry away unwanted water or waste from a building or street.
drains.example: Storm debris blocked the drains until the whole street flooded.

drama.definition: an exciting, emotional or tense series of events, or the art of acting and performing plays.
drama.example: Who is the announcer for tonight's drama finals?

dramatic.definition: very sudden, striking or exciting, in a way that catches everyone's attention.
dramatic.example: Does a dramatic headline always travel this fast?

drank.definition: swallowed a liquid, such as water or juice, by taking it into the mouth and throat.
drank.example: I drank some water to quell my cough so the presentation could continue smoothly.

drawing.definition: steadily attracting people or things towards itself, as though pulling them in.
drawing.example: Scientists observe an experiment closely before drawing any conclusions.

dread.definition: to feel strong worry or fear about something that is going to happen.
dread.example: My nerves usually abate the moment I begin speaking, so I no longer dread the opening line.

drew.definition: made a line, picture or shape using a pencil, pen or chalk.
drew.example: The teacher drew an oblique line on the board.

drift.definition: to move slowly and gradually away from the main topic or direction, without control.
drift.example: By 1948, whispers of independence had begun to drift across the continent like wind across long grass.

drifted.definition: moved slowly through the air or water, carried gently by a current or breeze.
drifted.example: A mild breeze drifted in from the sea.

drifting.definition: moving slowly and gradually, carried by wind, water or a current, without being pushed directly.
drifting.example: Jamal wrinkled his nose at the smell drifting from the kitchen.

drifts.definition: moves slowly and gradually, often without a clear direction, carried along by an outside force.
drifts.example: An accurate ear can detect when a single violin drifts out of tune among forty.

drill.definition: a practice exercise that trains people what to do in an emergency.
drill.example: Who dismantled the old barricade once the flood drill was finished?

drilling.definition: making a hole in a hard surface, such as rock or the ground, using a rotating tool.
drilling.example: The court ordered the mining company to desist from drilling near the protected waterfall.

drills.definition: sets of exercises repeated regularly to practise and improve a skill.
drills.example: I once loathed grammar drills, yet now I see how they quietly strengthened my writing.

drinking.definition: safe and suitable for people to drink, especially describing water.
drinking.example: Clean drinking water is an imperative for every settlement, large or small.

driver.definition: a person who controls and steers a vehicle such as a car, bus or lorry.
driver.example: The tired driver blinked hard to stay awake on the long road.

dropped.definition: fell or became lower in level, amount or position.
dropped.example: The oxygen levels have dropped again, Amara!

drought.definition: a long period of unusually dry weather during which there is little or no rainfall.
drought.example: Grandad still talks about farming here before the drought years, Maya!

drumbeat.definition: the sound made by hitting a drum, especially a single steady beat.
drumbeat.example: What makes a single drumbeat feel more ominous than a whole page of description?

drummer.definition: a person who plays the drums, especially in a band or orchestra.
drummer.example: Watch how quietly the drummer slips into the rhythm, Leo!

drummers.definition: people who play the drums, especially as part of a group.
drummers.example: Every festival brings poets and drummers into the old town square.

drumming.definition: the act of playing a set of drums, or the rhythmic sound this makes.
drumming.example: Thunderous drumming echoed through the hall during the opening scene.

drums.definition: musical instruments that are hit with hands or sticks to produce a rhythm.
drums.example: How would a string quartet render a song originally composed for drums alone?

drying.definition: becoming free of moisture or wetness, especially by being left in the air.
drying.example: "Consider this a gentle rebuke," said the teacher, pointing at the paint left drying on the brushes.

dub.definition: To give someone or something a name or title.
dub.example: What nickname will the fans dub the new mascot once it finally appears?

dull.example: The old paint had faded from green to a dull grey.

dumping.definition: the act of getting rid of unwanted material by leaving or throwing it somewhere, often carelessly or illegally.
dumping.example: Will the sea truly heal if people stop dumping waste into it?

dunes.definition: large mounds or ridges of sand shaped by the wind, especially in a desert.
dunes.example: The sand dunes kept shifting slightly with every strong gust of wind.

durable.definition: Able to last a long time without getting damaged.
durable.example: A durable routine outlasts any single burst of effort.

during.definition: throughout, or at some point within, a particular period of time.
during.example: Who blinked first during the staring contest?

dusk.definition: the time of day just before night, when daylight is fading.
dusk.example: I found the desolate playground at dusk strangely beautiful, though I wouldn't linger there alone.

dust.definition: fine, dry powder made up of tiny particles of dirt or other matter.
dust.example: Watch the dust spin over the ledge, Samira called out!

dwelling.definition: thinking or talking about something, especially something unpleasant, for longer than is helpful.
dwelling.example: Rather than dwelling on dismal news, I prefer studying communities that successfully restore their rivers.

eager.definition: very keen and enthusiastic to do or have something.
eager.example: Adam skipped lunch because he was so eager to hear the speech.

eagles.definition: large, powerful birds of prey with excellent eyesight, often found nesting on cliffs.
eagles.example: Only the wildlife authority can issue permits to film the eagles nesting on the cliffs.

earlier.definition: at a time before now, or before another event that is being discussed.
earlier.example: The land had been leased to a private firm months earlier.

earliest.definition: happening or made first, before all others of the same kind.
earliest.example: Mentors help young writers see the potential in their earliest drafts.

early.definition: before the usual, expected or planned time.
early.example: The bakery opens early every single morning.

earn.definition: to gain or deserve something as a result of effort, ability or good behaviour.
earn.example: Reviewers who mention a product's weaknesses tend to earn more trust.

earned.definition: gained or deserved something through effort, skill or good behaviour.
earned.example: A single false report can undo months of hard-earned trust.

earning.definition: gaining or deserving something as a reward for effort or achievement.
earning.example: In the scribes' guild, each subordinate copied manuscripts for years before earning a master's seal.

easier.definition: less difficult to do; requiring less effort.
easier.example: Are dried chickpeas easier to carry than fresh ones?

easily.example: Doubt slips away easily when a story sounds exciting enough.

east.definition: the direction from which the sun rises, opposite to west.
east.example: Which mountain range holds the highest peaks in East Africa?

easy.definition: not difficult; able to be done without much effort.
easy.example: An unsure voice is easy to spot in a crowded argument.

eating.definition: putting food into your mouth, chewing it and swallowing it.
eating.example: The group huddled in the shade, eating dried dates and roasted chickpeas while the heat shimmered on the stones below.

echo.definition: a sound that is reflected off a surface and heard again, slightly delayed and often fainter.
echo.example: Isn't it uncanny how folk tales from distant continents echo the very same warnings?

echoes.definition: produces or reflects sound repeatedly, so that it seems to continue after the original sound stops.
echoes.example: "This capacious hall echoes," noted the sound engineer, "so we'll need extra microphones."

eco.definition: relating to protecting the environment and reducing harm to nature.
eco.example: Does a green leaf on a label prove the product is actually eco-friendly?

ecological.definition: relating to the relationships between living things and their environment.
ecological.example: "Record the local dialect carefully," urged the linguist, "because each word preserves ecological knowledge."

economies.definition: the systems by which countries or regions produce, trade and use money, goods and resources.
economies.example: Entire fishing economies risk collapsing if the catch is never allowed to recover.

eddy.definition: A small, circular movement of water or air against the main flow
eddy.example: Can a kayaker really rest inside an eddy while the main current races past?

editing.definition: checking and improving a piece of writing by correcting mistakes and making changes.
editing.example: Sami, is that really censorship, or just responsible editing?

edition.definition: one of the particular versions in which a book, magazine or product is published or made available.
edition.example: I stayed indifferent to the limited-edition hype, and a week later the shelves were still full.

editor.definition: a person whose job is to check, correct and improve a piece of writing before it is published.
editor.example: The editor praised Amal's careful work on the article.

editors.definition: people whose job is to check, correct and improve pieces of writing before they are published.
editors.example: Many of the letters arrived unsigned, which worried the editors.

educate.definition: to teach someone so that they gain knowledge or understanding about something.
educate.example: I felt a flash of disdain for the tourists who littered beside the waterfall, then chose to educate rather than judge.

effect.definition: a change, result or impression that is caused by a particular action or event.
effect.example: Careful reporting can still produce a powerful, lasting effect.

effective.definition: successful in producing the result that was intended.
effective.example: What makes the wolf such an effective hunter in this landscape?

effectively.definition: in a way that produces the intended result; successfully.
effectively.example: Psychologists study emotion carefully so advertisers can use it more effectively.

effortless.definition: done easily, without seeming to need much effort or struggle.
effortless.example: What grace, Nora — the whole routine looked effortless!

efforts.definition: attempts or hard work made in order to achieve something.
efforts.example: Theo's quiet efforts accumulated into real change across the whole school.

egregious.definition: very bad or shocking; far beyond what anyone should accept
egregious.example: What punishment could possibly fit such an egregious breach of the public's trust?

elder.definition: an older person, especially one who is respected for their age, wisdom or experience.
elder.example: A gentle tone often persuades a nervous elder faster than a loud argument.

elder's.definition: belonging to an older person who is respected for their age, wisdom or experience.
elder's.example: The elder's stubborn refusal to change surprised even his own family.

elderly.definition: old, or relating to people who are old.
elderly.example: Walking the estate with the elderly residents gave the planners an entirely new perspective.

elders.definition: older people, especially those respected within a family or community for their wisdom or experience.
elders.example: Dare to dream of a bay as clear as the elders describe!

elders'.definition: belonging to a group of older, respected people.
elders'.example: Maya's initiative to record the elders' memories grew into a full school heritage project.

election.definition: an occasion when people vote to choose a person for a political or official position.
election.example: The election campaign lasted six weeks and ended with a debate in the town hall.

electric.definition: powered by a flow of energy carried through wires or batteries, rather than by petrol, diesel or muscle power.
electric.example: What obstacles slow the transition from petrol cars to electric vehicles in developing countries?

electricity.definition: a form of energy used to power lights, machines and appliances, carried through wires.
electricity.example: Why did the electricity cut during the busiest part of the day?

else.definition: in addition to, or different from, what has already been mentioned.
else.example: Sami ran faster than anyone else in the whole race!

elusive.definition: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve.
elusive.example: Why does the perfect balance between humour and honesty remain so elusive in advertising?

emaciated.definition: Very thin and weak because of not eating enough.
emaciated.example: Rescue workers fed the emaciated donkey until its strength returned.

email.definition: a written message sent electronically over the internet, or to send a message this way.
email.example: Was the strange email actually benign, or should Daniel report it to the ICT office?

emails.definition: written messages sent electronically over the internet.
emails.example: The station received dozens of emails after the broadcast aired.

embargo.definition: A law or order that stops trade or limits what can be sold.
embargo.example: Sami, tell us honestly what you heard about the embargo!

embarrassed.definition: feeling shy, awkward or ashamed, especially in front of other people.
embarrassed.example: "Hand it over; I must confiscate this catapult," said the warden to the embarrassed tourist.

embarrasses.definition: makes someone feel shy, awkward or ashamed, especially in front of others.
embarrasses.example: Looking back, my impudent remark to the visiting conductor embarrasses me, and I have since learned to question respectfully.

embarrassment.definition: a feeling of shyness, awkwardness or shame, especially caused by a mistake made in front of others.
embarrassment.example: Kian's face turned red with embarrassment after the joke.

embraced.definition: accepted or welcomed something new or different, especially eagerly.
embraced.example: Although I am conservative about changing my routines, I finally embraced digital flashcards and never looked back.

emerge.definition: To come out or appear from somewhere.
emerge.example: I watched my confidence emerge slowly this term, one presentation at a time.

emergency.definition: a sudden, serious and dangerous situation that needs immediate action.
emergency.example: Someone has to command during an emergency on the mountain.

emissions.definition: gases or substances released into the air, especially ones that are harmful to the environment.
emissions.example: Will global commitments falter when reducing emissions starts to demand genuine sacrifice?

emperor.definition: a male ruler of a large group of countries or territories controlled by one power.
emperor.example: Historians still debate whether the emperor could justify the enormous cost of his monuments.

emphasises.definition: gives special importance to something, to show that it matters a great deal.
emphasises.example: A careful reader should notice what each speaker emphasises, what each leaves out, and how each uses evidence.

empire's.definition: belonging to a large group of countries or territories ruled by a single power.
empire's.example: The empire's influence began to ebb long before its final ruler was crowned.

empties.definition: removes all the money, contents or people from something, leaving it with none.
empties.example: "Stay rational," said the chairperson gently; "anger fills the room but empties the budget."

emptiness.definition: the state or feeling of having nothing inside or nobody present; a sense of complete absence.
emptiness.example: I love opening a pristine notebook in September, though its emptiness is slightly terrifying too.

empty.example: A cold wind swept across the empty playground.

encouraged.definition: gave someone confidence or support to help them do something.
encouraged.example: Teacher Yasmin encouraged even the quietest students to talk openly.

encouragement.definition: words or actions that give someone confidence and support to keep trying.
encouragement.example: Theo received several nods of encouragement from the older students.

encourages.definition: gives someone confidence or a reason to do something.
encourages.example: How can parents instil habits of moderation in a world that constantly encourages waste?

end.definition: the final part or point of something, after which nothing more happens.
end.example: Even the sceptics agreed in the end, Amara!

endanger.definition: to put someone or something at risk of harm, damage or destruction.
endanger.example: Feeding the baboons will only antagonise the troop and endanger everyone on the trail.

endangered.definition: at risk of dying out or disappearing completely.
endangered.example: How many species are currently listed as endangered in this reserve?

ended.definition: came to a finish; stopped happening.
ended.example: Who ended up leading the club this term?

ending.definition: the final part of a story, film or event.
ending.example: It is completely normal to cry at a happy ending.

endless.definition: seeming to go on forever, without any limit or stopping point.
endless.example: The meadows look endless from up here, Leo said, gazing across the slopes!

endlessly.example: The map seemed to unfold endlessly as Sami tried to fold it back up.

endorsements.definition: public statements of support for a product, especially made by a famous person to persuade others to buy it.
endorsements.example: Reviews, testimonials, and celebrity endorsements all work on the idea of social proof.

ends.definition: finishes, or comes to a close.
ends.example: Every unit in this course ends with a short quiz.

endurance.definition: the ability to keep going through something difficult or tiring for a long time.
endurance.example: The advert filmed the car crossing a desolate salt flat to emphasise its endurance.

enforced.definition: made sure that a law, rule or agreement was actually obeyed and followed.
enforced.example: But here, in the hills of northern Tanganyika, silence was still enforced — through rules, expectations, and fear.

engine.definition: the part of a vehicle or machine that produces power to make it move or work.
engine.example: The engine hums quietly as the bus climbs the hill.

engineers.definition: people trained to design, build or repair machines, structures or systems.
engineers.example: No plans had been released, and no engineers were named.

engross.definition: To completely focus on something and not notice anything else.
engross.example: Old maps engross me for hours; every border hides a story someone rarely tells.

engrossed.definition: so interested and absorbed in something that you notice nothing else around you.

enjoyed.definition: got pleasure or satisfaction from doing or experiencing something.
enjoyed.example: Amal enjoyed working alongside the nurse at the busy clinic.

enjoys.definition: gets pleasure or satisfaction from doing or experiencing something.
enjoys.example: Grandma Hana enjoys sipping coffee slowly on the veranda each morning.

enormous.definition: extremely large in size or amount.
enormous.example: Wow, Idris, the new library is enormous!

enrolling.definition: officially joining a course, school or organisation as a member or student.
enrolling.example: The steep course fees did not deter me from enrolling; I simply saved for a whole year.

ensemble.definition: a group of musicians, actors or dancers who perform together.
ensemble.example: The whole ensemble moved onstage together, exactly as they had rehearsed.

enter.definition: to go or come into a place.
enter.example: Idris, that is your cue to enter!

entering.definition: going or coming into a place.
entering.example: Purification alone will not help if the pollution keeps entering upstream.

entertainment.definition: activities, performances or events that are designed to amuse or interest people.
entertainment.example: I find it repugnant when talent shows humiliate contestants merely for entertainment.

enthusiasm.definition: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something.
enthusiasm.example: The pattern of enthusiasm fading after a few weeks was familiar to Jamal.

entire.definition: whole; with no part left out.
entire.example: Wow, the entire student body cheered at once!

entirely.example: The choice to click share or not is entirely yours.

entries.definition: items, such as pieces of work, that are submitted to take part in a competition.
entries.example: "We received a multitude of entries," beamed the judge, "far beyond last year's design contest."

envelope.definition: a flat paper container used to hold and post a letter or document.
envelope.example: Who left the envelope in your locker, Kofi?

envy.definition: a feeling of wanting what someone else has, such as their success, possessions or qualities.
envy.example: Is it possible to exult in a classmate's success without feeling a flicker of envy?

epic.definition: a long story or poem, often traditional, that tells of heroic deeds and adventures.
epic.example: Reciting an entire epic from memory demands stamina as well as artistry.

episode.definition: one single part of a television or radio programme that is broadcast in a series.

equal.definition: the same in amount, size, value or status as something else.
equal.example: Nora, the sailors traded spice and stories in equal measure!

eroded.definition: gradually worn away by the action of water, wind or weather over time.
eroded.example: What keeps volunteers returning each summer to such gruelling work on the eroded terraces?

erratic.example: The weather has been erratic, changing from sunny to rainy quickly.

error.definition: a mistake, especially one made carelessly or through lack of knowledge.
error.example: Maya took full responsibility for the error in her report!

errors.definition: mistakes, especially ones made carelessly or through lack of knowledge.
errors.example: The team worked on simplifying the sorting code to fix its errors.

escalated.definition: became rapidly more serious, intense or out of control.
escalated.example: "I had to intervene before the glue gun argument escalated," laughed the technology teacher.

escaped.definition: got away or came out despite an effort to hold it back or keep it hidden.
escaped.example: I tried to look impassive when my design won, but my grin escaped within seconds.

escaping.definition: getting away from a dangerous, unpleasant or unwanted situation or place.
escaping.example: Why does the poster pair a desolate landscape with the slogan about escaping the crowd?

especially.definition: more than usual, or more than in other cases; particularly.
especially.example: The dry season made the fields especially easy to set alight.

essay.definition: a short piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for school or college.
essay.example: What rich vocabulary that essay had, Sami!

essays.definition: short pieces of writing on a particular subject, especially ones written for school or college.
essays.example: The students type their essays on the library computers.

estate.definition: a large area of land with many houses built on it, usually planned and built together.
estate.example: Why is the bus service so sporadic on the estate where residents need it most?

estimated.definition: worked out an approximate value or amount for something, without measuring it exactly.
estimated.example: Eratosthenes estimated the circumference of the Earth using shadows and simple geometry.

evacuations.definition: occasions when people are moved away quickly from a dangerous place to somewhere safer.
evacuations.example: Would earlier warnings hasten evacuations enough to keep riverside families safe?

even.definition: used to show that something is surprising, or that it goes further than what would normally be expected.
