trips.definition: journeys made to particular places, especially for a short time.
trips.example: Should teachers confiscate phones during field trips, or teach students to use them responsibly?

triumphant.definition: feeling or expressing great joy or pride after achieving a victory or success.
triumphant.example: The melody seems to meander like a river before gathering into the triumphant chorus.

triumphs.definition: great successes or victories, especially ones achieved after significant effort.
triumphs.example: The biography's conclusion argues that the inventor's failures taught him more than his triumphs.

troop.definition: a group of animals, especially monkeys or baboons, that live and move around together
troop.example: Feeding the baboons will only antagonise the troop and endanger everyone on the trail.

trophies.definition: cups or other prizes given to the winners of a competition or contest
trophies.example: The winners brandish their trophies while the crowd cheers from the stands.

trophy.definition: a cup or other object given as a prize for winning a competition or contest
trophy.example: Is this trophy really ours, or did the judges make a mistake?

troubled.definition: caused someone to feel worried, upset or uneasy about something
troubled.example: I watched glossy branding usurp honest labelling on that shelf, and it genuinely troubled me.

troubling.definition: causing someone to feel anxious, upset or uneasy
troubling.example: What a troubling thought that was, Nora!

troupe.definition: a group of actors, dancers or other performers who work and travel together
troupe.example: After the exhausting festival tour, the theatre troupe travelled to the coast to recuperate.

trudged.definition: walked slowly and heavily, especially because you were tired, unhappy or exhausted
trudged.example: The team trudged home dejected after the final whistle.

true.definition: in accordance with fact; genuine, real and not invented, exaggerated or temporary
true.example: What is the true source of this claim?

truly.definition: in a real, sincere or complete way, rather than only appearing to be so
truly.example: Does a truly great story always make someone cry?

trust.definition: believe that someone or something is honest, reliable and will not cause harm or deceive you
trust.example: That footage is far too blurry to trust, Milo!

trusted.definition: believed that someone or something was honest, reliable or safe
trusted.example: I thank every caller who trusted us with their story.

truth.definition: the facts of a situation, especially as opposed to what is invented, exaggerated or believed

truths.definition: facts or ideas that are correct and real, especially ones that are important or uncomfortable to accept
truths.example: How did the jester's antics deliver truths that the king refused to hear from anyone else?

try.definition: make an effort to do something, without being certain that you will succeed

trying.definition: making an effort to do, achieve or improve something, even though success is not guaranteed
trying.example: Imani refused to let shame stop her from trying again.

tune.definition: a sequence of musical notes that forms a pleasant or recognisable melody
tune.example: A familiar tune can offer comfort even when the words make no sense.

tuning.definition: adjusting a musical instrument so that it produces the correct pitch
tuning.example: How accurate is the old metronome compared with the tuning app on your phone?

tunnel.definition: a long passage, often underground or enclosed, that leads from one place to another
tunnel.example: "The jellyfish were faintly luminous," whispered Theo, describing the aquarium's darkened tunnel.

turned.definition: moved so as to face a different direction, or changed into a different state or thing
turned.example: The sky turned orange and pink at sunrise.

turning.definition: changing direction, or changing something into a different form or state
turning.example: Rohan scoffed when Milo suggested turning back.

turnout.definition: the number of people who attend an event or take part in something, such as voting
turnout.example: "The turnout was dismal," admitted Adam, "but the ten volunteers who came worked brilliantly."

turns.definition: changes someone or something so that they become different or take on a new form
turns.example: Which particle turns watch into watch out?

tutor.definition: a person who teaches one student or a small group, often outside a regular school class
tutor.example: "Let your improvisation meander a little," encouraged the tutor, "and see where it leads you."

twice.definition: on two separate occasions, or in an amount twice as large as before
twice.example: Which student declined the invitation twice?

twins.definition: two children born to the same mother at the same time
twins.example: The twins share an uncanny ability to finish each other's stories without missing a beat.

twist.definition: an unexpected change or surprising development, especially in the plot of a story
twist.example: "She faked every single injury!" gasped the audience during the twist.

typo.definition: a small mistake in a piece of writing or typing, such as a wrong or missing letter
typo.example: "I should have proofread my letter," said Adam with a rueful laugh, holding up the typo.

tyrants.definition: cruel or unjust rulers who have total power over the people they govern
tyrants.example: Folk tales often motivate listeners by showing ordinary people outwitting powerful tyrants.

umpire's.definition: belonging to the official who makes sure players follow the rules in a sport
umpire's.example: Why did the umpire's emphatic signal end the argument before it truly began?

unanswered.definition: not yet given a reply, solution or explanation, and so still open to question
unanswered.example: I dislike wasting discussion time on a quibble when larger questions about meaning remain unanswered.

uncanny.definition: Strange or mysterious, often in a way that is unsettling.
uncanny.example: Isn't it uncanny how folk tales from distant continents echo the very same warnings?

uncle.definition: the brother of your mother or father, or the husband of your aunt
uncle.example: Imagine, Omar's uncle was once elected to parliament!

uncovered.definition: found something that had been hidden, buried or kept secret, especially by digging or investigating
uncovered.example: Years of digging finally uncovered who had leased the land.

underpass.definition: a passage or road that goes underneath another road, railway or path
underpass.example: "Your exuberant mural has transformed this grey underpass," the mayor told the delighted art club.

underrated.definition: not valued or appreciated as highly as it actually deserves
underrated.example: I believe patience is an underrated tactic when you are trying to change people's habits.

understand.definition: know the meaning of something, or grasp why or how something is true
understand.example: Did the council understand the seriousness of the situation?

understanding.definition: knowledge or comprehension of what something means or how it works
understanding.example: Reciting a script is easy; understanding it is much harder.

understood.definition: knew and grasped the meaning of something that was said, done or seen
understood.example: Amal read the letter twice to be certain she understood it.

undisturbed.definition: left alone, without being touched, interrupted or interfered with in any way
undisturbed.example: How quickly can a forest replenish itself after a fire, if it is left undisturbed?

undulate.definition: To move in waves or with a smooth, wavy motion.
undulate.example: Why do desert dunes undulate in patterns that look deliberately designed from the air?

undulating.definition: moving gently up and down or from side to side in a smooth, wave-like way
undulating.example: I filmed the flags undulating above the stalls and used the clip to open our market documentary.

unfair.definition: not fair, reasonable or equal in the way people are treated
unfair.example: How unfair it was to quote just half of her sentence!

unfinished.definition: not yet completed, finished or brought to a proper conclusion
unfinished.example: A missed rehearsal can leave a whole scene unfinished.

unforgettable.definition: so remarkable or memorable that no one could fail to remember it
unforgettable.example: Samira meandered along the beach, and the sunset made it unforgettable!

universe.definition: the whole of space and everything in it, including all the planets, stars and galaxies
universe.example: Staring at the desert sky, I felt the infinite scale of the universe press gently on my imagination.

unkind.definition: behaving in a way that is unpleasant, hurtful or lacking consideration for other people's feelings
unkind.example: I still feel rueful about the unkind remark I made before learning the full story.

unless.definition: except if; only if something else happens or turns out to be true
unless.example: It's theirs now, Imani, not ours, unless we speak up today!

unlocked.definition: made it possible to access, understand or make use of something previously out of reach
unlocked.example: I made the shrewd decision to learn root words, which unlocked dozens of new terms at once.

unnoticed.definition: without being seen or attracting anyone's attention
unnoticed.example: A stranger offering large sums of money rarely goes unnoticed for long.

unread.definition: never looked at or gone through by anyone, especially a piece of writing
unread.example: I keep my emails succinct now, having learnt that long messages simply go unread.

unremarkable.definition: ordinary and not especially interesting, impressive or unusual
unremarkable.example: Training for the relay taught me that stamina grows quietly, one unremarkable session at a time.

unsafe.definition: dangerous or likely to cause harm, injury or an accident
unsafe.example: Severe pollution near the factory has made the river unsafe to drink.

unsettled.definition: made someone feel anxious or uneasy, or disrupted something that had previously been calm or stable
unsettled.example: The strange pull towards the old house unsettled every visitor.

unusual.definition: not common or ordinary; different from what would normally be expected
unusual.example: What was that unusual smell coming from the harbour?

unwritten.definition: generally understood and followed by everyone, even though it has never been officially recorded on paper
unwritten.example: Exchange students gradually accustom themselves to new idioms, unfamiliar accents and unwritten rules of conversation.

update.definition: bring something up to date by adding new information or making changes to it
update.example: How can a community update its doctrine of stewardship without losing the wisdom inside it?

upgrade.definition: a change that improves something, such as equipment or a system, making it more modern or effective
upgrade.example: "Your password system is obsolete," warned the technician, "and an upgrade cannot wait."

uproar.definition: a loud, excited or angry reaction from a group of people; noisy confusion or protest
uproar.example: I find my grandfather's benign presence calming, even when the whole household is in uproar.

ups.definition: the second part of the word clean-ups, referring to organised sessions in which volunteers collect litter and tidy a place
ups.example: Trust her, Sami, her experience with clean-ups is worth listening to!

upstream.definition: in the direction against the flow of a river, towards where it begins
upstream.example: Could the pollution really be coming from somewhere further upstream?

urged.definition: strongly encouraged, advised or pushed someone to do something, often with real urgency
urged.example: Speak truthfully, Imani urged the class, even when the truth is unpopular!

usage.definition: the amount of something, such as water or electricity, that is consumed, or the way something is employed
usage.example: Can you check my arithmetic before I hand in the water-usage report?

use.definition: put something into service or apply it in order to achieve a particular purpose
use.example: What a clever use of adverbs in that description!

used.definition: employed or applied something in order to achieve a particular purpose or result
used.example: What bold superlatives that headline used!

useful.definition: helpful and practical, serving a clear purpose or making a task easier
useful.example: That is genuinely useful information, Nora!

using.definition: employing or applying something as a means of doing something else
using.example: Can you form a conditional using the words if and would?

usually.definition: most of the time, or in the way something normally or typically happens
usually.example: What do you usually do on the eve of an exam?

usurp.definition: To take control of something, especially a position of power, without the right to do so.
usurp.example: I let social media usurp my reading time last term, a mistake I refuse to repeat.

utterly.definition: completely and totally, used to emphasise the full extent of something, especially something negative
utterly.example: From the shore, the water looked perfectly blue and utterly calm.

vague.definition: not clearly or precisely expressed, described or stated
vague.example: A vague answer often conceals more than it reveals.

valley.definition: a low area of land between hills or mountains, often with a river running through it
valley.example: At last, Idris, we have peace in the valley!

valuable.definition: very useful, important or beneficial, and therefore worth having or paying attention to
valuable.example: Teacher Yasmin called the library the school's most valuable resource!

value.definition: the importance, usefulness or worth that something or someone has, especially compared with the cost involved
value.example: The elders said we'd understand the bay's value only once it was gone.

vandals.definition: people who deliberately damage or destroy property, especially for no good reason
vandals.example: The team trudged home dejected after vandals wrecked the flowerbeds they had planted.

vanilla.definition: a sweet flavour, popular in ice cream and desserts, made from the pods of a tropical plant

vanish.definition: disappear suddenly and completely, often without any warning or clear explanation
vanish.example: Imani felt her nerves vanish the moment she walked onstage.

vanished.definition: disappeared suddenly and completely, often without any warning or clear explanation
vanished.example: The loose stone spun off the ledge and vanished below!

vans.definition: medium-sized road vehicles used for transporting goods or equipment
vans.example: The librarian led a tireless campaign to bring mobile book vans to the distant villages.

vegetables.definition: plants or parts of plants, such as carrots or cabbages, that are grown and eaten as food
vegetables.example: Idris pushed the wooden cart loaded with fresh vegetables.

vehicles.definition: machines, such as cars or lorries, used to transport people or goods from one place to another
vehicles.example: What obstacles slow the transition from petrol cars to electric vehicles in developing countries?

velvet.definition: a soft, thick fabric with a smooth, slightly furry surface on one side
velvet.example: Samira admired the richest fabric backstage, all velvet and gold.

vendor's.definition: belonging to a person who sells goods, especially from a stall or in the street
vendor's.example: The vendor's stall sat near the edge of the garden gate.

venue.definition: the place where an event, such as a concert or meeting, takes place
venue.example: "Officers will apprehend anyone selling forged tickets," announced the venue manager firmly.

verdict.definition: an official decision or judgement, especially one reached after careful consideration
verdict.example: What silence was creeping over the hall before the final verdict!

verify.definition: check that something is true, accurate or correct
verify.example: A willing witness makes a story far easier to verify.

verse.definition: one of the sections of a song or poem, usually with a regular rhythm or rhyme
verse.example: Why does the chorus sound so repetitive by the final verse?

verses.definition: sections of a song or poem, each usually following a similar pattern of rhythm or rhyme
verses.example: Who was the muse behind the songwriter's most tender verses about home?

vests.definition: sleeveless garments worn over other clothes, sometimes for safety or as an extra layer
vests.example: The safety vests use luminous strips so cyclists remain visible on the darkest winter mornings.

vet.definition: a doctor who is trained to treat sick or injured animals
vet.example: "The lump proved benign," the vet assured Maya, "so your cat needs only rest."

veteran.definition: a person who has a great deal of experience in a particular activity or job
veteran.example: "Weeding is tedious until you notice the robins following you," smiled the allotment veteran.

veterinary.definition: relating to the medical treatment of sick or injured animals
veterinary.example: Volunteering at the sanctuary helped kindle in me an ambition to study veterinary science.

victims.definition: people who have been harmed, injured or badly affected by an event such as a disaster or crime
victims.example: Why does public concern for flood victims wane so quickly once the cameras leave?

victory.definition: an act of winning a contest, game or struggle against an opponent
victory.example: Planting a new mangrove sapling felt like a small victory.

video.definition: a recording of moving images, often with sound, that can be watched on a screen
video.example: How can you tell if a video is fake, Sami?

view.definition: the range of scenery that can be seen from a particular place, especially one that is attractive
view.example: The view from the outcrop was undeniably beautiful.

viewers.definition: people who watch something, such as a television programme, film or advertisement
viewers.example: Trained critics detect small flaws that most viewers miss.

views.definition: a person's opinions or beliefs about a particular subject
views.example: Had his views already hardened before he heard the other side?

village's.definition: belonging to a small community of houses in the countryside
village's.example: What kind of flood destroys a whole village's written records?

villagers.definition: people who live in a small rural community
villagers.example: Many villagers feared the rising tide long before the flood came.

villagers'.definition: belonging to the people who live in a small rural community
villagers'.example: The haughty official dismissed the villagers' concerns without reading their carefully prepared petition.

villages.definition: small communities of houses, usually in the countryside, smaller than a town
villages.example: The charity works to end hunger in coastal villages, Sami.

villain.definition: the main bad or evil character in a story, film or play
villain.example: The film's evil villain manipulated the news for his own gain.

vine.definition: a climbing plant with a long stem, often grown for its grapes or as decoration
vine.example: The vine clung to the crumbling wall for support, didn't it?

violation.definition: an act of breaking or failing to respect a law, rule or agreement
violation.example: Dumping chemical waste into the protected wetlands was an egregious violation of the environmental agreement.

violin.definition: a wooden musical instrument with four strings, played by drawing a bow across them and held under the chin
violin.example: An accurate ear can detect when a single violin drifts out of tune among forty.

violinist.definition: a person who plays a wooden musical instrument with four strings, held under the chin and played with a bow
violinist.example: The famous violinist seemed aloof backstage, yet spent an hour teaching children afterwards.

viral.definition: spreading very quickly among many people, especially online through shares and links
viral.example: The viral protest was traced to a hoax flyer that Kian had shared without checking.

visible.definition: able to be seen clearly, especially from a distance or in poor light
visible.example: The safety vests use luminous strips so cyclists remain visible on the darkest winter mornings.

vision.definition: the ability to think about or plan the future with imagination and wisdom
vision.example: Which attribute of a great leader matters most during an environmental crisis: honesty or vision?

visit.definition: an occasion of going to see a person or place for a period of time
visit.example: Nora, you visit the library so often these days!

visiting.definition: going to see a person or place, especially one you do not live at or belong to
visiting.example: Amal spent her holiday visiting three museums in one week.

visitor.definition: a person who comes to see a particular place or person
visitor.example: The hospital asked every visitor to wash with soap first.

visitors.definition: people who come to see a particular place or person
visitors.example: Who swept the classroom before the visitors came?

visits.definition: occasions of going to see a particular person or place for a period of time
visits.example: Muddy paw prints on the doorstep were the telltale evidence of the fox's nightly visits.

vital.definition: extremely important or necessary, especially for something to work or succeed
vital.example: I admire the cunning of mystery writers who hide the vital clue in plain sight.

vocal.definition: relating to the human voice, especially in singing
vocal.example: "Nerves can sabotage a performance faster than any rival," warned the vocal coach.

voiced.definition: expressed a feeling, opinion or complaint openly, usually by speaking about it
voiced.example: Residents voiced their exasperation when the promised playground repairs were postponed a third time.

voices.definition: the sounds produced by a person's throat and mouth when speaking or singing
voices.example: Come and participate, Sami, we need more voices!

voicing.definition: expressing a feeling, opinion or objection in words
voicing.example: I have learnt that voicing dissent calmly persuades far more people than staying resentfully silent.

volcanoes.definition: mountains with an opening at the top through which lava, gas and ash can erupt
volcanoes.example: What first kindled your fascination with the volcanoes of the Rift Valley?

volume.definition: the loudness of a sound, or the control used to make it louder or quieter
volume.example: "Your argument needs evidence, not volume," the debate coach reminded the excitable second speaker.

volunteer.definition: a person who offers to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced to
volunteer.example: Each volunteer took a turn collecting rubbish from the rocks.

volunteer's.definition: belonging to a person who offers to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced to
volunteer's.example: Dejection was written across every volunteer's face after the storm ruined the clean-up.

volunteered.definition: offered to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced to
volunteered.example: Teacher Yasmin was grateful when her students volunteered for the clean-up.

volunteering.definition: doing work, usually unpaid, to help other people or a cause, without being forced to
volunteering.example: Volunteering at the sanctuary helped kindle in me an ambition to study veterinary science.

volunteers.definition: people who offer to do something, especially unpaid work, without being forced to
volunteers.example: The volunteers were helping to clear the flooded street.

vote.definition: a formal way of choosing or deciding something, in which people indicate their preference, for example by raising a hand or marking a paper
vote.example: Next month, parliament will vote on the education bill.

voted.definition: made a formal choice among options, for example by raising a hand or marking a paper
voted.example: The board voted to expel the boy after the third warning.

vulnerable.definition: Easily hurt or harmed, either physically or emotionally.
vulnerable.example: Being rendered vulnerable onstage taught Rohan to trust his own instincts.

waft.definition: To move gently through the air, often describing smells or sounds.
waft.example: How does the sound of the bell waft so clearly across the water at dawn?

wafted.definition: moved gently and slowly through the air, carried by a light breeze
wafted.example: Songs from my neighbour's radio wafted through my window and slipped into the poem I was writing.

wait.definition: stay in a place or delay doing something until a particular time or event
wait.example: Sami, wait for me on the corner!

wakes.definition: stops sleeping and becomes conscious, especially after a night's rest
wakes.example: Idris trains every morning before the rest of the town wakes.

waking.definition: the act of stopping sleeping and becoming conscious again, especially in the morning

walker.definition: a person moving on foot, especially in a race or organised event
walker.example: The exuberant crowd cheered every runner, from the record-setter to the exhausted final walker.

walking.definition: moving from place to place on foot, at a normal, unhurried speed
walking.example: Amal said it, jaw tight, before walking away from the group.

walkway.definition: a path or passage, often raised or paved, made for people to move along on foot
walkway.example: "Move the display boards so they don't obstruct the walkway," instructed the exhibition organiser.

wall.definition: an upright structure, usually made of brick or stone, that encloses, divides or supports something
wall.example: Watch out, Theo, that old wall is collapsing!

wallow.definition: To stay in a feeling or situation for a long time, often a negative one.
wallow.example: Why wallow in disappointment when the next audition is only a month away?

wander.definition: move around an area without any fixed direction or purpose
wander.example: Good writers control their sentences instead of letting them wander.

wane.definition: To become smaller, less strong, or less important over time.
wane.example: Interest in the recycling scheme began to wane once the posters came down.

want.definition: have a desire for something or wish to do something
want.example: Why would anyone want to block the only exit?

wanted.definition: had a desire for something or wished to do something
wanted.example: Nobody wanted to swim in water this polluted, Sami!

war.definition: a period of fighting between countries or groups, usually using armed forces
war.example: Which colonies gained independence first after the war?

warden.definition: a person responsible for supervising or protecting a particular place, such as a nature reserve
warden.example: Set the limit low and enforce it, the warden says.

warden's.definition: belonging to a person responsible for supervising or protecting a particular place
warden's.example: Her mind spun with questions after the warden's announcement.

warehouse.definition: a large building used for storing goods before they are sold or distributed
warehouse.example: Whose tip led the investigation towards the abandoned warehouse, Kofi?

warm.definition: having a pleasantly high temperature, or, when describing a person or feeling, friendly and affectionate
warm.example: The lamp gave off a warm, steady light.

warmer.definition: higher in temperature; hotter than before or than something else
warmer.example: Warmer water holds less oxygen than cooler water does.

warmly.definition: in a friendly, enthusiastic or affectionate manner that shows genuine kindness towards someone
warmly.example: Why do audiences respond so warmly when an artist dares to be vulnerable on stage?

warmth.definition: the quality of having a comfortably high temperature, or a feeling of being pleasantly hot
warmth.example: I try to make rational choices about transport, though I admit the bus's warmth sways me in January.

warned.definition: told someone about a possible danger, problem or unpleasant consequence in advance
warned.example: Amal warned that the claim might be exaggerated.

warning.definition: a statement, sign or event that tells people of a possible danger or problem before it happens
warning.example: The signal cut without any warning at all.

warnings.definition: statements or signs that tell people of a possible danger or problem before it happens
warnings.example: Was the reef really killed by years of ignored warnings?

washing.definition: cleaning something, especially clothes or fabric, using water and often soap
washing.example: Volunteers monitor the beach each morning for signs of oil washing ashore.

waste.definition: unwanted material or rubbish that is thrown away after being used
waste.example: What a waste of good fruit crates, Sami!

wasted.definition: used carelessly, without good purpose, or in a way that achieves nothing useful
wasted.example: Notice the precision of that gesture, Idris - not a single movement is wasted!

wasteful.definition: using more time, money or materials than necessary, leaving some with no useful purpose
wasteful.example: Choose the least wasteful option, Sami, even if it looks less exciting!

wastes.definition: uses time, money or materials carelessly, without gaining any real benefit from them
wastes.example: Could you give a more precise figure for how much water the school wastes each week?

wasting.definition: using time, money or resources carelessly, without any useful result
wasting.example: A smart design solves a problem without wasting extra parts.

watch.definition: look at something, such as a film or event, and pay attention to it
watch.example: Watch me dive from the rocks, Omar!

watched.definition: looked at something and observed what was happening
watched.example: Zara watched as he limped slowly toward the gates!

watching.definition: looking at something and paying attention to what is happening
watching.example: "You are calm," he added, watching her steady hands.

watchtower.definition: a tall structure built to allow someone to see over a wide area and look out for danger
watchtower.example: Where does this steep trail culminate: at the waterfall or at the ancient watchtower?

watchtowers.definition: tall structures built to allow people to see over a wide area and look out for danger
watchtowers.example: Ancient watchtowers jut from the coastline like sentences left deliberately unfinished.

waterfall.definition: a place where a stream or river flows over a steep drop, such as a cliff, and falls to the ground below
waterfall.example: Visitors travel for days just to glimpse the magnificent waterfall at dawn.

waterhole.definition: a natural pool of water in a dry area, where animals go to drink
waterhole.example: How did such an astute negotiator persuade both farmers and rangers to share the waterhole?

waterproof.definition: made in a way that does not let water pass through, so it stays dry or undamaged
waterproof.example: Volunteers will affix waterproof labels to every recycling bin on the pier.

waves.definition: curved ridges of water that move across the surface of the sea or a lake, especially caused by wind
waves.example: Outside, clouds undulated in waves across the sky.

waving.definition: moving something, such as your hand or an object, from side to side in the air, often as a greeting
waving.example: "This auction is a bonanza for collectors," declared the presenter, waving the catalogue.

way.definition: a particular method, style or manner in which something is done or happens
way.example: Nora walked beside Amal on the way to school.

we'll.definition: a short way of writing or saying 'we will', used before a verb to talk about the future
we'll.example: "This capacious hall echoes," noted the sound engineer, "so we'll need extra microphones."

weak.definition: lacking strength, power or effectiveness; not able to withstand pressure or scrutiny
weak.example: What makes a strong story different from a weak rumour?

weaken.definition: make something less strong, powerful or effective
weaken.example: Was Nadir planting doubts to weaken the team's confidence?

weakest.definition: having the least strength, power or effectiveness among a group being compared
weakest.example: The slickest adverts often hide the weakest evidence behind them.

wealthy.definition: having a great deal of money, property or valuable possessions; rich
wealthy.example: Wealthy nations often fill their museums with documents and artefacts.

weaving.definition: combining different things together skilfully, especially by including them throughout a piece of writing or work
weaving.example: I chose to commemorate my grandmother in my capstone poem, weaving her sayings into every stanza.

website.definition: a set of related pages on the internet that can be viewed using a web browser
website.example: Every caption on the school website is checked by a teacher.

websites.definition: sets of related pages on the internet that can be viewed using a web browser
websites.example: I now cite historians rather than random websites, and my arguments have grown noticeably stronger.

wedding.definition: a ceremony and celebration at which two people get married
wedding.example: The band's sound is a bold concoction of desert blues, jazz, and traditional wedding songs.

weeds.definition: wild plants that grow where they are not wanted, often crowding out other plants
weeds.example: Samira spent the afternoon picking weeds from between the garden stones.

weekend.definition: Saturday and Sunday, the days at the end of the week when many people do not work or go to school
weekend.example: Amal wants to add a turtle to the mural this weekend.

weekends.definition: Saturdays and Sundays, the days at the end of the week when many people do not work or go to school
weekends.example: Leo loves spending his weekends exploring nature near the river!

weeks.definition: periods of seven days each, used to measure and organise time
weeks.example: This whole town has been dry for weeks, Sami!

weighing.definition: carefully considering different facts or possibilities before reaching a decision
weighing.example: They practised weighing evidence, questioning sources, and respecting viewpoints different from their own.

weighs.definition: carefully considers and compares different facts before reaching a decision
weighs.example: Look at this new shell, Leo — it barely weighs anything!

welcome.definition: greet someone in a warm and friendly way, especially when they arrive
welcome.example: Sign up for the weekly forum, Daniel, everyone is welcome!

welcoming.definition: gladly accepting or receiving something or someone in a warm, friendly way
welcoming.example: What a welcoming environment this forum has become, Nora!

went.definition: moved, progressed or developed in a particular way
went.example: Was the interview shortened before it went on air?

west.definition: the direction towards which the sun sets, or the region lying in that direction
west.example: Musicologists often compare the pentatonic scales of West Africa and East Asia.

wetland.definition: an area of low land that is often flooded or covered in shallow water, such as a marsh or swamp
wetland.example: Are we making any real headway against the invasive weeds choking the wetland?

wetlands.definition: areas of low land that are often flooded or covered in shallow water, such as marshes or swamps
wetlands.example: Can the company support its claim that the pipeline caused no damage to the wetlands?

whatever.definition: anything that; used to say something applies no matter what the circumstances are
whatever.example: A family must eat today, whatever happens to the mountain tomorrow.

whenever.definition: at any time that something happens, or on every occasion that it does
whenever.example: Amal and Nora clap along whenever the chorus repeats.

whisper.definition: a very quiet way of speaking, using only breath rather than the voice
whisper.example: One vendor near the garden gate lowered her voice to a whisper.

whispered.definition: spoke very quietly, using breath rather than the voice
whispered.example: Adam whispered, "That line was flat, wasn't it?"

whispers.definition: quiet remarks or pieces of information, often secretive, passed from person to person
whispers.example: Amal could hear whispers about the embargo all through the corridor.

whole.definition: complete; including every part of something
whole.example: The whole hall roared its approval, Nadir!

widely.definition: to a great extent or over a large range
widely.example: Sami read the correction, and he shared it widely as well!

wildflower.definition: a flower that grows naturally in the countryside rather than being deliberately planted
wildflower.example: "This is not freedom; it is anarchy," said the warden, surveying the trampled wildflower meadow.

wildlife.definition: wild animals and plants living in their natural environment
wildlife.example: The class walked through the forest to study the local wildlife.

win.definition: succeed in a competition, contest or struggle against others
win.example: And that, she thought, was how to win with integrity.

wind.definition: air that moves naturally, especially strongly, across the earth's surface
wind.example: A raw wind blew in off the water that evening.

windswept.definition: exposed to strong winds, often giving an open, bare or battered appearance
windswept.example: What made this windswept plateau suitable for habitation when the fertile valley lay empty?

wing.definition: one of the limbs a bird, insect or bat uses to fly
wing.example: "I deplore cruelty in every form," said the vet, bandaging the injured stork's wing.

winners.definition: people who succeed in a competition or contest
winners.example: How long had the crowd waited before the winners were finally announced?

winning.definition: achieving first place or victory in a competition or contest
winning.example: Who framed the winning photograph for the exhibition?

wins.definition: achieves success or victory, or gains something as a result of a contest or effort
wins.example: A patient advocate wins more support than an angry one.

winter.definition: the coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring
winter.example: How many sheep does the farm keep during the winter?

wire.definition: a thin strand or thread of metal, often used to carry electricity or to support something
wire.example: Who twisted the wire into such a strange shape?

wisely.definition: in a sensible way that shows good judgement
wisely.example: How can one shopper choose wisely when facing a multitude of confusing eco-labels?

wish.definition: want something to happen or be true, especially something not currently possible or not yet certain
wish.example: What a brilliant idea, Nora, I wish we had thought of it sooner!

withdrawn.definition: taken away or removed, especially something that had been provided or promised
withdrawn.example: Would the reserve descend into anarchy if the rangers' funding were suddenly withdrawn?

witnesses.definition: people who see an event happen, especially one such as a crime or accident
witnesses.example: Are these two witnesses truly independent of each other?

wizard.definition: a person, especially in stories, believed to have magical powers; also used for someone remarkably skilled at something

woke.definition: stopped sleeping and became awake, or, figuratively, suddenly became alert and interested
woke.example: The buses hummed past as the harbour city woke up.

won.definition: achieved first place or victory in a contest or competition
won.example: Who won the debating contest last year?

won't.definition: a short way of writing or saying 'will not', used before a verb to talk about the future
won't.example: "I won't chastise you for trying something bold," said the mentor, "only for hiding the results."

wonder.definition: a feeling of great amazement, admiration or awe, often caused by something impressive or beautiful
wonder.example: Each wonder is gruelling to reach, magnificent to see and surprisingly easy to harm.

wooden.definition: made of wood, or having the appearance, texture or colour of wood
wooden.example: How many props can fit inside that old wooden crate?

woodworm.definition: the larvae of a beetle that bore into and damage wood, or the damage they cause
woodworm.example: I noticed the telltale sawdust below the beam and reported the woodworm before real damage spread.

words.definition: units of language that people use, spoken or written, to express meaning
words.example: Incredible, her words carried such weight!

wore.definition: had something on your body as clothing or a covering
wore.example: Is that the same shirt you wore to the summit last month?

worked.definition: did a job, task or made an effort towards achieving something
worked.example: Teacher Yasmin has worked at this school for ten years.

workers.definition: people who do a job, especially in a factory, on a building site or in another manual role
workers.example: Nora watched the workers tipping sand into the mixer.

workers'.definition: belonging to people who do a job, especially manual labour
workers'.example: The affluent merchant funded a library so that the dock workers' children could study in the evenings.

works.definition: functions correctly or successfully, or operates in the way it is intended to
works.example: Which method works faster, a checklist or a gut feeling?

workshop.definition: a meeting or session in which a group of people learn about or practise a particular skill
workshop.example: Picture a multi-storey workshop full of ideas, Rohan!

workshops.definition: rooms or buildings where things are made or repaired, or sessions in which people learn or practise a skill
workshops.example: Why not avail yourself of the free workshops on composting that the community centre offers?

world.definition: the earth, together with all its countries, peoples and natural features
world.example: Questioning who made a message and why is essential in today's world.

world's.definition: belonging to the earth and all its countries and peoples
world's.example: Why do the world's oldest myths teem with rivers, serpents, and impossible journeys?

worlds.definition: imagined or distinct places, settings or realms, especially created in a story or in space
worlds.example: A skilled narrator can conjure infinite worlds from a handful of ordinary words.

worried.definition: feeling or showing anxiety or unease about something, or causing someone to feel this way
worried.example: Tell me what's happening, Sami, you look worried!

worries.definition: feelings of anxiety or unease about something, or the problems that cause them
worries.example: The dissolved oxygen reading worries me, Teacher Yasmin!

worry.definition: feel anxious or uneasy about something, especially something that might go wrong
worry.example: It's only a minor problem, Sami, don't worry!

worth.definition: having a value or benefit that makes something deserving of the time, effort or cost involved
worth.example: Relax your fist, Amal, he isn't worth the anger!

worthwhile.definition: valuable, useful or important enough to justify the time, effort or cost spent on it
worthwhile.example: When I compare my first recital tape with this year's, the progress makes every early struggle worthwhile.

wouldn't.definition: a short way of writing or saying 'would not', often used to talk about something that will not or did not happen
wouldn't.example: Wouldn't it be nice if the bay stayed clear all year?

woven.definition: made by crossing threads or strips of material over and under each other, or, figuratively, skilfully combined from many parts
woven.example: The poster's intricate border, woven from tiny product images, rewarded viewers who looked closely.

wrap.definition: a material, such as plastic or paper, used to cover or enclose something
wrap.example: Look at all this plastic, Nora, just to wrap one tiny toy!

wrapped.definition: covered something by winding or folding material around it
wrapped.example: The vine wrapped its tendril around the fence to climb higher.

wrappers.definition: pieces of paper, plastic or other material used to cover and protect food or products, usually thrown away after use
wrappers.example: Plastic wrappers are a common sight along this stretch of coast.

wrapping.definition: covering or enclosing something by winding or folding material around it
wrapping.example: "The situation is dire but not hopeless," the vet said, wrapping the injured owl.

wreak.definition: cause a great amount of damage, harm or trouble
wreak.example: How much havoc can one faulty microphone wreak during a live broadcast?

wrecked.definition: badly damaged, broke apart or completely destroyed something, often deliberately
wrecked.example: The team trudged home dejected after vandals wrecked the flowerbeds they had planted.

wrist.definition: the joint that connects the hand to the arm, allowing the hand to bend and rotate
wrist.example: "My broken wrist was a hindrance," admitted Sami, "but the team adjusted the prototype schedule."

writer's.definition: belonging to a person who produces books, articles, stories or other texts
writer's.example: A single passage can reveal a writer's whole style.

writers.definition: people who produce books, articles, stories or other texts as their work or interest
writers.example: Young writers often mix fact with a little imagination.

writing.definition: the activity of forming letters and words to record language, or the text produced this way
writing.example: Imani had been writing since she was ten years old.

written.definition: produced by forming letters and words on a page rather than spoken aloud
written.example: I had to decipher the secret message written in code.

wrong.definition: incorrect, mistaken, or not as intended or expected
wrong.example: Amal, reread that sentence, something feels wrong!

wrote.definition: created a piece of text, such as a letter, essay or book, by forming words on a page
wrote.example: What plain, powerful prose that essayist wrote!

year.definition: a period of twelve months, or a group of pupils who are taught together at the same stage of school
year.example: Who won the debating contest last year?

year's.definition: belonging to or happening during a specific period of twelve months
year's.example: What should we place inside this year's time capsule?

yearbook.definition: a book published every twelve months, often by a school, recording events, students and achievements from that period
yearbook.example: A printing defect left twenty copies of the yearbook without their final, most important page.

yearbooks.definition: books published every twelve months, often by a school, recording events, students and achievements from that period
yearbooks.example: "Let no setback deter you," wrote the headteacher in our yearbooks, "least of all a single grade."

yearly.definition: happening or done once every twelve months, on a regular annual basis
yearly.example: The village treasured its yearly festival of music and poetry.

years.definition: periods of time lasting twelve months each
years.example: A forest can take a hundred years to grow back.

yoghurt.definition: a thick, slightly sour food made from milk that has fermented with bacteria

young.definition: being in an early stage of life; not old, whether describing a person, animal or plant
young.example: The museum displayed a portrait of the young queen.

younger.definition: less old than someone or something else being compared
younger.example: Nora is helping the younger students with their reading.

youngest.definition: the least old, or the smallest in age, among a group
youngest.example: Did the youngest actor remember his bow at the end?

yourself.definition: used to refer back to the person being spoken to, when they are both the subject and object of an action, or for emphasis
yourself.example: Stop proving yourself, Sami, we already trust you!

yourselves.definition: used to refer back to the group of people being spoken to, when they are both the subject and object of an action, or for emphasis
yourselves.example: Believe in yourselves, Sami, the odds are not against us yet!

youth.definition: the period of a person's life when they are young, or young people considered as a group
youth.example: Was that really your grandson standing beside the youth group, Jamal?

zeal.definition: A strong feeling of enthusiasm and eagerness.
zeal.example: His voice, raw with zeal, carried right across the crowded street.
